report.headline: Usage projected to climb from 17.6% in the NBA to 23.1% in the EuroLeague, but the accompanying shooting-efficiency projection carries no signal

projection.text: Usage rate is projected to rise from 17.6% in the NBA to 23.1% in the EuroLeague, moving from below the NBA average to above the EuroLeague's minutes-weighted average of 20.0%.

risks.text: Turnover rate in the source season was elevated at 21.0%, a risk that could compound if usage rises as projected.

Source-season shooting efficiency was below the NBA average (51.5% true shooting, -0.53 sd), and the projected rebound to 56.5% comes from a model that is no better than the league-mean baseline (4.7% error both ways) and carries no real signal.
The 95% usage interval (16.3%-30.0%) covers roughly three EuroLeague standard deviations, so the model can rank this player among cohort peers but cannot pin down an individual outcome.
The estimate rests on 115 historical NBA->EL transitions of players who, conditional on making the move, sat only 0.31 standard deviations below their own league's average, a modest selection margin.

strengths.text: Source-season playmaking was strong: a 28.7% assist rate and 7.033 assists per 75 possessions.

The usage-rate model beats its trivial baseline (3.3% mean absolute error vs 4.3%), and the fitted NBA->EL slope of 0.982 shows nearly all of a player's relative standing carries over, giving the projected rise to 23.1% real weight.
The projected usage rate of 23.1% sits above the EuroLeague's minutes-weighted average of 20.0%, consistent with a EuroLeague role built on greater ball-handling responsibility.

uncertainty.text: The 80% prediction interval for usage (18.6%-27.6%) spans two full standard deviations of the EuroLeague usage distribution (SD 4.5%), and the true shooting percentage projection (56.5%) comes from a model that is no better than the simple league-average baseline (4.7% error either way), so that number should not be treated as informative.
